hedges.reason: The most common way the primary fails is Likud falling into the low 20s while Together passes it. A 20-24 seat count for Likud pays exactly in those worlds.

For Likud to lose first place, its seat count almost has to fall below 30, because no opposition list can realistically clear 30 while Yashar and The Democrats run separately. This leg pays in every failure world, and also in the many primary-win worlds where Likud wins with 25-29.

This is the closest instrument on the list to my hedge thesis: a centrist government led by Bennett. If Together comes first, Bennett gets the first claim on forming a coalition and the strongest case for the premiership.

claims.reason: If Likud is not first, another single list outscored it. With the opposition split across Together, Yashar, The Democrats and the Arab lists, no rival list reaches 31 or more seats. So Likud losing first place means Likud is below 30. In the other failure path, a postponed or indeterminate election, there is no certified 30-34 result for Likud either.
